```{r}
cat("N =", nrow(trans14_surv), "\n")

cat(
  "Correlation between risk score and P(HESN) =",
  cor(
    trans14_surv$trans14_risk,
    trans14_surv$trans14_prob_hesn
  ),
  "\n"
)

cat("\nP(HESN) range:\n")
print(
  range(
    trans14_surv$trans14_prob_hesn
  )
)

cat("\nRisk score summary:\n")
print(
  summary(
    trans14_surv$trans14_risk
  )
)

## =============================================================================
## 4. FINAL TRANS14 RISK SCORE TERTILES
## =============================================================================

q_trans14 <- quantile(
  trans14_surv$trans14_risk,
  probs = c(0, 1/3, 2/3, 1),
  na.rm = TRUE
)

trans14_surv$trans14_tercile <- cut(
  trans14_surv$trans14_risk,
  breaks = q_trans14,
  labels = c(
    "T1_LowRisk",
    "T2_MedRisk",
    "T3_HighRisk"
  ),
  include.lowest = TRUE
)

cat("\n============================================================\n")
cat("--- EVENTS BY RISK TERTILE — FINAL TRANS14 ---\n")
cat("============================================================\n")

print(
  table(
    trans14_surv$trans14_tercile,
    trans14_surv$event
  )
)

print(
  trans14_surv %>%
    group_by(trans14_tercile) %>%
    summarise(
      N = n(),
      Events = sum(event),
      Censored = sum(event == 0),
      Event_rate = mean(event),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
)

## =============================================================================
## 5. KAPLAN–MEIER AND LOG-RANK ANALYSIS — FINAL TRANS14
## =============================================================================

trans14_surv_obj <- Surv(
  time  = trans14_surv$TTS,
  event = trans14_surv$event
)

trans14_logrank <- survdiff(
  trans14_surv_obj ~ trans14_tercile,
  data = trans14_surv
)

trans14_logrank_p <- pchisq(
  trans14_logrank$chisq,
  df = length(trans14_logrank$n) - 1,
  lower.tail = FALSE
)

cat("\n============================================================\n")
cat("--- LOG-RANK TEST — FINAL TRANS14 ---\n")
cat("============================================================\n")

print(trans14_logrank)

cat(
  "\np =",
  format.pval(
    trans14_logrank_p,
    digits = 6,
    eps = 1e-300
  ),
  "\n"
)
```

```{r}
trans14_beta_tt   <- coef(trans14_cox_tv)["tt(trans14_risk_z)"]

      trans14_V[
        "trans14_risk_z",
        "tt(trans14_risk_z)"
      ]

    se_logHR <- sqrt(var_logHR)

    data.frame(
      Time_days = t,
      HR = exp(logHR),
      Lower_95CI =
        exp(logHR - 1.96 * se_logHR),
      Upper_95CI =
        exp(logHR + 1.96 * se_logHR)
    )
  }
)
```

## Analysis clustering genes HESN-UP

```{r}


library(biomaRt)
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)
library(ggplot2)

## =============================================================================
## GENOMIC CLUSTERING ANALYSIS OF HESN-UPREGULATED GENES
## =============================================================================

## 1. LOAD DIFFERENTIALLY EXPRESSED GENE LISTS

hesn_file <- file.path(getwd(), "DESeq2_HESN_up_noCell.tsv")
hiv_file <- file.path(getwd(), "DESeq2_HIV_up_noCell.tsv")

stopifnot(file.exists(hesn_file), file.exists(hiv_file))

hesn_deg <- read.delim(hesn_file, check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
hiv_deg <- read.delim(hiv_file, check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

gene_col <- intersect(c("Gene", "gene", "gene_symbol", "hgnc_symbol", "SYMBOL", "Symbol"), intersect(names(hesn_deg), names(hiv_deg)))
if (!length(gene_col)) stop("Gene symbol column not identified.")
gene_col <- gene_col[1]

clean_genes <- function(x) {
  x <- unique(trimws(as.character(x)))
  x[!is.na(x) & nzchar(x)]
}

genes_HESN_up <- clean_genes(hesn_deg[[gene_col]])
genes_HIV_up <- clean_genes(hiv_deg[[gene_col]])

## Preserve aliases used by downstream analyses
genes_HESN <- genes_HESN_up
genes_HIV <- genes_HIV_up

stopifnot(identical(genes_HESN, genes_HESN_up))
stopifnot(identical(genes_HIV, genes_HIV_up))

cat("HESN-UP:", length(genes_HESN), "\n")
cat("HIV-UP:", length(genes_HIV), "\n")




## =============================================================================
## 2. RETRIEVE GENOMIC COORDINATES FROM LOCAL ENSEMBL ANNOTATION
## =============================================================================

library(ensembldb)
library(EnsDb.Hsapiens.v86)
library(dplyr)

## Ensembl release 86, GRCh38
edb <- EnsDb.Hsapiens.v86::EnsDb.Hsapiens.v86

## Retrieve gene coordinates from the local database
coords_all <- ensembldb::genes(
  edb,
  columns = c("gene_id", "gene_name", "seq_name", "gene_seq_start", "gene_seq_end", "seq_strand", "gene_biotype"),
  return.type = "DataFrame"
) %>%
  as.data.frame()

## Format genomic coordinates for the original clustering pipeline
coords_HESN <- coords_all %>%
  dplyr::transmute(
    hgnc_symbol = as.character(gene_name),
    ensembl_gene_id = as.character(gene_id),
    chromosome_name = as.character(seq_name),
    start_position = as.numeric(gene_seq_start),
    end_position = as.numeric(gene_seq_end),
    strand = as.character(seq_strand),
    gene_biotype = as.character(gene_biotype)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    hgnc_symbol %in% genes_HESN &
    chromosome_name %in% c(as.character(1:22), "X", "Y")
  ) %>%
  dplyr::distinct(hgnc_symbol, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(
    factor(chromosome_name, levels = c(as.character(1:22), "X", "Y")),
    start_position
  )

genes_missing <- setdiff(genes_HESN, coords_HESN$hgnc_symbol)

cat("HESN-UP genes:", length(genes_HESN), "\n")
cat("Mapped genes:", nrow(coords_HESN), "\n")
cat("Unmapped genes:", length(genes_missing), "\n")
print(genes_missing)


## =============================================================================
## 3. IDENTIFY GENOMIC CLUSTERS BASED ON INTERGENIC DISTANCE
## =============================================================================

# Define genomic clusters using a maximum intergenic distance threshold
assign_clusters <- function(coords, max_gap = 1e6) {

  coords %>%
    arrange(
      factor(
        chromosome_name,
        levels = c(as.character(1:22), "X", "Y")
      ),
      start_position
    ) %>%
    group_by(chromosome_name) %>%
    mutate(
      previous_end = dplyr::lag(cummax(end_position)),

      gap_bp = start_position - previous_end,

      new_cluster =
        is.na(previous_end) |
        gap_bp > max_gap,

      cluster_num = cumsum(new_cluster)
    ) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    mutate(
      cluster_id =
        paste0("chr", chromosome_name, "_C", cluster_num)
    )
}

# Assign genomic clusters using a maximum gap of 1 Mb
coords_1Mb <- assign_clusters(
  coords_HESN,
  max_gap = 1e6
)

## =============================================================================
## 4. ANNOTATE GENE FAMILIES
## =============================================================================

# Classify genes into major gene families based on HGNC symbol patterns
coords_1Mb <- coords_1Mb %>%
  mutate(
    GeneFamily = case_when(

      grepl("^OR[0-9]", hgnc_symbol) ~ "Olfactory receptor",

      grepl("^TRAV|^TRBV|^TRGV|^TRDV",
            hgnc_symbol) ~ "TCR",

      grepl("^IGH|^IGK|^IGL",
            hgnc_symbol) ~ "Immunoglobulin",

      grepl("^HBA|^HBB|^HBD$|^HBM$",
            hgnc_symbol) ~ "Globin",

      grepl("^KRTAP",
            hgnc_symbol) ~ "Keratin-associated protein",

      grepl("^KRT[0-9]",
            hgnc_symbol) ~ "Keratin",

      grepl("^SPRR",
            hgnc_symbol) ~ "SPRR",

      grepl("^LCE",
            hgnc_symbol) ~ "LCE",

      grepl("^ZNF",
            hgnc_symbol) ~ "Zinc-finger",

      grepl("^PCDH",
            hgnc_symbol) ~ "Protocadherin",

      grepl("^HIST",
            hgnc_symbol) ~ "Histone",

      TRUE ~ "Other"
    )
  )


## =============================================================================
## 5. SUMMARIZE GENOMIC CLUSTERS
## =============================================================================

cluster_summary <- coords_1Mb %>%
  dplyr::group_by(chromosome_name, cluster_id) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    n_genes = dplyr::n(),
    cluster_start = min(start_position),
    cluster_end = max(end_position),
    span_Mb = (cluster_end - cluster_start) / 1e6,
    genes = paste(hgnc_symbol, collapse = ", "),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(n_genes >= 2) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(n_genes), chromosome_name, cluster_start)

print(cluster_summary, n = Inf)
View(cluster_summary)


```


## Statistical permutation test for genomic clustering enrichment


```{r}
################################################################################
## GENOMIC CLUSTERING + PERMUTATION TEST
## HESN-UP vs HIV-UP
##
## Primary cluster definition:
## - same chromosome
## - at least 3 genes
## - distance between consecutive genes <= 1 Mb
##
## Null model:
## - same number of genes per chromosome as the observed gene set
## - sampling from the actual background of genes tested by DESeq2
################################################################################

library(biomaRt)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(tibble)

## =============================================================================
## 1. GLOBAL PARAMETERS
## =============================================================================

MAX_GAP <- 1e6
MIN_CLUSTER_SIZE <- 3
B_PERM <- 10000



## =============================================================================
## 2. DESEQ2 INPUTS
## =============================================================================

library(dplyr)
library(ensembldb)
library(EnsDb.Hsapiens.v86)

background_genes <- unique(rownames(dds))

hesn_deg <- read.delim("DESeq2_HESN_up_noCell.tsv", check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
hiv_deg <- read.delim("DESeq2_HIV_up_noCell.tsv", check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

gene_col <- intersect(c("Gene", "gene", "gene_symbol", "hgnc_symbol", "SYMBOL", "Symbol"), intersect(names(hesn_deg), names(hiv_deg)))
if (!length(gene_col)) stop("Gene symbol column not identified.")
gene_col <- gene_col[1]

clean_genes <- function(x) {
  x <- unique(trimws(as.character(x)))
  x[!is.na(x) & nzchar(x)]
}

genes_HESN_up <- clean_genes(hesn_deg[[gene_col]])
genes_HIV_up <- clean_genes(hiv_deg[[gene_col]])
genes_HESN <- genes_HESN_up
genes_HIV <- genes_HIV_up

cat("Background:", length(background_genes), "\n")
cat("HESN-UP:", length(genes_HESN_up), "\n")
cat("HIV-UP:", length(genes_HIV_up), "\n")

## =============================================================================
## 3. LOCAL ENSEMBL GRCh38 ANNOTATION
## =============================================================================

edb <- EnsDb.Hsapiens.v86::EnsDb.Hsapiens.v86

coords_all <- as.data.frame(ensembldb::genes(
  edb,
  columns = c("gene_id", "gene_name", "seq_name", "gene_seq_start", "gene_seq_end", "seq_strand", "gene_biotype"),
  return.type = "DataFrame"
)) %>%
  dplyr::transmute(
    hgnc_symbol = as.character(gene_name),
    chromosome_name = as.character(seq_name),
    start_position = as.numeric(gene_seq_start),
    end_position = as.numeric(gene_seq_end),
    band = NA_character_,
    gene_biotype = as.character(gene_biotype),
    ensembl_gene_id = as.character(gene_id)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(hgnc_symbol), nzchar(hgnc_symbol), chromosome_name %in% c(as.character(1:22), "X", "Y")) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(hgnc_symbol, chromosome_name, start_position, ensembl_gene_id) %>%
  dplyr::distinct(hgnc_symbol, .keep_all = TRUE)

## =============================================================================
## 4. RETRIEVE COORDINATES WITHOUT BIOMART
## =============================================================================

get_coords <- function(genes, coords_reference = coords_all) {
  coords_reference %>%
    dplyr::filter(hgnc_symbol %in% unique(genes))
}

coords_background <- get_coords(background_genes)

cat("Background genes with genomic coordinates:", nrow(coords_background), "\n")
cat("Unmapped background genes:", length(setdiff(background_genes, coords_background$hgnc_symbol)), "\n")

## Ensure observed genes belong to the mapped testing universe
missing_HESN_background <- setdiff(genes_HESN_up, coords_background$hgnc_symbol)
missing_HIV_background <- setdiff(genes_HIV_up, coords_background$hgnc_symbol)

cat("HESN-UP outside mapped background:", length(missing_HESN_background), "\n")
cat("HIV-UP outside mapped background:", length(missing_HIV_background), "\n")



## =============================================================================
## 5. FUNCTION TO ASSIGN PHYSICAL GENOMIC CLUSTERS
## =============================================================================

assign_clusters <- function(coords, max_gap = 1e6) {

  coords %>%
    dplyr::arrange(
      factor(
        chromosome_name,
        levels = c(as.character(1:22), "X", "Y")
      ),
      start_position,
      end_position
    ) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(
      chromosome_name
    ) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(

      previous_end =
        dplyr::lag(end_position),

      gap_bp =
        start_position - previous_end,

      # Start a new cluster if:
      # 1) this is the first gene on the chromosome
      # 2) the gap from the previous gene exceeds max_gap
      new_cluster =
        is.na(previous_end) |
        gap_bp > max_gap,

      cluster_number =
        cumsum(new_cluster)

    ) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup() %>%
    dplyr::mutate(

      cluster_id =
        paste0(
          "chr",
          chromosome_name,
          "_C",
          cluster_number
        )
    )
}


## =============================================================================
## 6. GENOMIC CLUSTERING METRICS
## =============================================================================

get_cluster_metrics <- function(
    coords,
    max_gap = 1e6,
    min_cluster_size = 3
) {

  x <- assign_clusters(
    coords,
    max_gap = max_gap
  )

  cluster_sizes <- x %>%
    dplyr::count(
      chromosome_name,
      cluster_id,
      name = "n_genes"
    )

  valid_clusters <- cluster_sizes %>%
    dplyr::filter(
      n_genes >= min_cluster_size
    )

  n_clustered <- sum(
    valid_clusters$n_genes
  )

  tibble::tibble(

    n_total_genes =
      nrow(x),

    n_clusters =
      nrow(valid_clusters),

    n_clustered_genes =
      n_clustered,

    proportion_clustered =
      n_clustered / nrow(x),

    max_cluster_size =
      ifelse(
        nrow(valid_clusters) == 0,
        0,
        max(valid_clusters$n_genes)
      )
  )
}


## =============================================================================
## 7. EMPIRICAL P-VALUE
## =============================================================================

empirical_p <- function(
    null_values,
    observed
) {

  (
    sum(
      null_values >= observed
    ) + 1
  ) /
    (
      length(null_values) + 1
    )
}


## =============================================================================
## 8. CHROMOSOME-MATCHED RANDOM SAMPLING
## =============================================================================

sample_chr_matched <- function(
    coords_background,
    chr_counts
) {

  sampled_list <- lapply(
    seq_len(nrow(chr_counts)),

    function(i) {

      chr_i <-
        chr_counts$chromosome_name[i]

      n_i <-
        chr_counts$n_target[i]

      pool <- coords_background %>%
        dplyr::filter(
          chromosome_name == chr_i
        )

      if (nrow(pool) < n_i) {

        stop(
          paste0(
            "Insufficient background genes on chr ",
            chr_i,
            ". Required: ",
            n_i,
            " genes; available: ",
            nrow(pool),
            "."
          )
        )
      }

      pool %>%
        dplyr::slice_sample(
          n = n_i,
          replace = FALSE
        )
    }
  )

  dplyr::bind_rows(
    sampled_list
  )
}


## =============================================================================
## 9. MAIN ANALYSIS FUNCTION
## =============================================================================

run_clustering_test <- function(
    target_genes,
    label,
    coords_background,
    B = 10000,
    max_gap = 1e6,
    min_cluster_size = 3,
    seed = 12345
) {

  cat("\n============================================================\n")
  cat("ANALYSIS:", label, "\n")
  cat("============================================================\n")

  ## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  ## 9.1 Genomic coordinates
  ## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  
## Use the same genomic universe for observed and permuted genes
coords_target <- get_coords(target_genes, coords_background)

missing_genes <- setdiff(target_genes, coords_target$hgnc_symbol)

cat("Original genes:", length(target_genes), "\n")
cat("Mapped genes:", nrow(coords_target), "\n")
cat("Unmapped genes:", length(missing_genes), "\n")


  cat("Original genes:",
      length(target_genes), "\n")

  cat("Genes with genomic coordinates:",
      nrow(coords_target), "\n")

  cat("Genes without genomic coordinates:",
      length(missing_genes), "\n")

  if (length(missing_genes) > 0) {

    write.table(
      data.frame(
        gene = missing_genes
      ),
      paste0(
        label,
        "_genes_without_coordinates.tsv"
      ),
      sep = "\t",
      quote = FALSE,
      row.names = FALSE
    )
  }


  ## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  ## 9.2 Observed genomic clustering
  ## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  obs <- get_cluster_metrics(
    coords_target,
    max_gap = max_gap,
    min_cluster_size = min_cluster_size
  )

  cat("\nObserved genomic clustering:\n")
  print(obs)


  ## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  ## 9.3 Detailed table of observed clusters
  ## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  coords_clustered <- assign_clusters(
    coords_target,
    max_gap = max_gap
  )

  cluster_summary <- coords_clustered %>%
    dplyr::group_by(
      chromosome_name,
      cluster_id
    ) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(

      n_genes =
        dplyr::n(),

      cluster_start =
        min(start_position),

      cluster_end =
        max(end_position),

      span_bp =
        cluster_end - cluster_start,

      span_Mb =
        span_bp / 1e6,

      max_gap_kb =
        ifelse(
          dplyr::n() > 1,
          max(
            gap_bp[-1],
            na.rm = TRUE
          ) / 1000,
          NA_real_
        ),

      median_gap_kb =
        ifelse(
          dplyr::n() > 1,
          median(
            gap_bp[-1],
            na.rm = TRUE
          ) / 1000,
          NA_real_
        ),

      cytobands =
        paste(
          unique(band),
          collapse = "; "
        ),

      genes =
        paste(
          hgnc_symbol,
          collapse = ", "
        ),

      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    dplyr::filter(
      n_genes >= min_cluster_size
    ) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(
      dplyr::desc(n_genes),
      chromosome_name,
      cluster_start
    )


  ## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  ## 9.4 Gene-level table of genes belonging to qualifying clusters
  ## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  clustered_genes <- coords_clustered %>%
    dplyr::semi_join(
      cluster_summary %>%
        dplyr::select(
          cluster_id
        ),
      by = "cluster_id"
    ) %>%
    dplyr::select(
      chromosome_name,
      cluster_id,
      hgnc_symbol,
      band,
      start_position,
      end_position,
      gap_bp,
      gene_biotype
    ) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(
      chromosome_name,
      cluster_id,
      start_position
    )


  ## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  ## 9.5 Chromosomal distribution
  ## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  chr_counts <- coords_target %>%
    dplyr::count(
      chromosome_name,
      name = "n_target"
    )


  ## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  ## 9.6 Permutations
  ## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  set.seed(seed)

  perm_results <- vector(
    mode = "list",
    length = B
  )

  cat(
    "\nStarting",
    B,
    "chromosome-matched permutations...\n"
  )

  for (b in seq_len(B)) {

    random_coords <-
      sample_chr_matched(
        coords_background,
        chr_counts
      )

    perm_results[[b]] <-
      get_cluster_metrics(
        random_coords,
        max_gap = max_gap,
        min_cluster_size = min_cluster_size
      )

    if (b %% 1000 == 0) {

      cat(
        label,
        ":",
        b,
        "/",
        B,
        "\n"
      )
    }
  }

  perm_results <-
    dplyr::bind_rows(
      perm_results
    )


  ## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  ## 9.7 Empirical p-values
  ## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  p_clusters <-
    empirical_p(
      perm_results$n_clusters,
      obs$n_clusters
    )

  p_clustered_genes <-
    empirical_p(
      perm_results$n_clustered_genes,
      obs$n_clustered_genes
    )

  p_prop_clustered <-
    empirical_p(
      perm_results$proportion_clustered,
      obs$proportion_clustered
    )

  p_max_cluster <-
    empirical_p(
      perm_results$max_cluster_size,
      obs$max_cluster_size
    )


  ## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  ## 9.8 Statistical summary
  ## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  permutation_summary <- tibble::tibble(

    Metric = c(
      paste0(
        "Number of clusters (≥",
        min_cluster_size,
        " genes)"
      ),

      paste0(
        "Number of genes contained in clusters (≥",
        min_cluster_size,
        " genes)"
      ),

      paste0(
        "Proportion of genes contained in clusters (≥",
        min_cluster_size,
        " genes)"
      ),

      "Maximum cluster size"
    ),

    Observed = c(
      obs$n_clusters,
      obs$n_clustered_genes,
      obs$proportion_clustered,
      obs$max_cluster_size
    ),

    Null_Mean = c(
      mean(
        perm_results$n_clusters
      ),
      mean(
        perm_results$n_clustered_genes
      ),
      mean(
        perm_results$proportion_clustered
      ),
      mean(
        perm_results$max_cluster_size
      )
    ),

    Null_SD = c(
      sd(
        perm_results$n_clusters
      ),
      sd(
        perm_results$n_clustered_genes
      ),
      sd(
        perm_results$proportion_clustered
      ),
      sd(
        perm_results$max_cluster_size
      )
    ),

    Empirical_P = c(
      p_clusters,
      p_clustered_genes,
      p_prop_clustered,
      p_max_cluster
    )
  )

  cat("\nPermutation test results:\n")
  print(
    permutation_summary
  )


  ## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  ## 9.9 Main figure
  ## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  p <- ggplot(
    perm_results,
    aes(
      x = n_clustered_genes
    )
  ) +
    geom_histogram(
      bins = 40,
      boundary = 0
    ) +
    geom_vline(
      xintercept =
        obs$n_clustered_genes,
      linetype = "dashed",
      linewidth = 1
    ) +
    annotate(
      "text",
      x =
        obs$n_clustered_genes,
      y = Inf,

      label =
        paste0(
          "Observed = ",
          obs$n_clustered_genes,
          "\nEmpirical p = ",
          signif(
            p_clustered_genes,
            3
          )
        ),

      vjust = 1.5,
      hjust = 1.05
    ) +
    labs(
      title =
        paste0(
          "Genomic clustering — ",
          label
        ),

      subtitle =
        paste0(
          B,
          " chromosome-matched permutations; ",
          "cluster ≥ ",
          min_cluster_size,
          " genes; gap ≤ ",
          max_gap / 1e6,
          " Mb"
        ),

      x =
        paste0(
          "Genes located in clusters of ≥",
          min_cluster_size,
          " genes"
        ),

      y =
        "Permutation count"
    ) +
    theme_classic(
      base_size = 12
    )


  print(p)


  ## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  ## 9.10 Export results
  ## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  prefix <- gsub(
    "[^A-Za-z0-9]+",
    "_",
    label
  )

  write.table(
    cluster_summary,
    paste0(
      prefix,
      "_physical_clusters_min",
      min_cluster_size,
      "_gap",
      max_gap / 1e6,
      "Mb.tsv"
    ),
    sep = "\t",
    quote = FALSE,
    row.names = FALSE
  )

  write.table(
    clustered_genes,
    paste0(
      prefix,
      "_clustered_genes_min",
      min_cluster_size,
      "_gap",
      max_gap / 1e6,
      "Mb.tsv"
    ),
    sep = "\t",
    quote = FALSE,
    row.names = FALSE
  )

  write.table(
    permutation_summary,
    paste0(
      prefix,
      "_permutation_summary_min",
      min_cluster_size,
      "_gap",
      max_gap / 1e6,
      "Mb.tsv"
    ),
    sep = "\t",
    quote = FALSE,
    row.names = FALSE
  )

  write.table(
    perm_results,
    paste0(
      prefix,
      "_permutation_raw_min",
      min_cluster_size,
      "_gap",
      max_gap / 1e6,
      "Mb.tsv"
    ),
    sep = "\t",
    quote = FALSE,
    row.names = FALSE
  )

  ggsave(
    paste0(
      prefix,
      "_clustering_permutation_min",
      min_cluster_size,
      "_gap",
      max_gap / 1e6,
      "Mb.pdf"
    ),
    plot = p,
    width = 8,
    height = 5
  )


  ## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  ## 9.11 Return analysis objects
  ## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  return(
    list(
      coordinates = coords_target,
      clustered_coordinates = coords_clustered,
      clusters = cluster_summary,
      clustered_genes = clustered_genes,
      observed = obs,
      permutations = perm_results,
      summary = permutation_summary,
      plot = p
    )
  )
}


## =============================================================================
## 10. RUN HESN-UP ANALYSIS
## =============================================================================

res_HESN_cluster <- run_clustering_test(
  target_genes = genes_HESN_up,
  label = "HESN_UP",
  coords_background = coords_background,
  B = B_PERM,
  max_gap = MAX_GAP,
  min_cluster_size = MIN_CLUSTER_SIZE,
  seed = 20260824
)


## =============================================================================
## 11. RUN HIV-UP ANALYSIS
## =============================================================================

res_HIV_cluster <- run_clustering_test(
  target_genes = genes_HIV_up,
  label = "HIV_UP",
  coords_background = coords_background,
  B = B_PERM,
  max_gap = MAX_GAP,
  min_cluster_size = MIN_CLUSTER_SIZE,
  seed = 20260825
)


## =============================================================================
## 12. FINAL HESN vs HIV COMPARISON
## =============================================================================

comparison <- dplyr::bind_rows(

  res_HESN_cluster$observed %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      Group = "HESN-UP"
    ),

  res_HIV_cluster$observed %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      Group = "HIV-UP"
    )

) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    Group,
    dplyr::everything()
  )

cat("\n============================================================\n")
cat("FINAL COMPARISON: HESN-UP vs HIV-UP\n")
cat("============================================================\n")

print(comparison)
view(comparison)


## =============================================================================
## 13. DISPLAY CLUSTERS IN R
## =============================================================================

cat("\n============================================================\n")
cat("HESN-UP CLUSTERS\n")
cat("============================================================\n")

print(
  res_HESN_cluster$clusters,
  n = Inf
)

cat("\n============================================================\n")
cat("HIV-UP CLUSTERS\n")
cat("============================================================\n")

print(
  res_HIV_cluster$clusters,
  n = Inf
)
```

```{r}
################################################################################
## FINAL GENOMIC CLUSTER SUMMARY: HESN-UP + HIV-UP

library(dplyr)

## 1. Extract genomic clusters

  dplyr::mutate(Group = "HESN-UP")

## 2. Combine HESN-UP and HIV-UP clusters

  dplyr::select(
    Group,
    chromosome_name,
    cluster_id,
    n_genes,
    cluster_start,
    cluster_end,
    span_Mb,
    max_gap_kb,
    median_gap_kb,
    cytobands,
    genes
  ) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(
    factor(Group, levels = c("HESN-UP", "HIV-UP")),
    dplyr::desc(n_genes),
    chromosome_name,
    cluster_start
  )

## 3. Display the complete genomic cluster table
print(
  clusters_final,
  n = Inf,
  width = Inf
)

## 4. Export results as TSV
write.table(
  clusters_final,
  file = "Genomic_clusters_HESN_vs_HIV_min3_gap1Mb.tsv",
  sep = "\t",
  quote = FALSE,
  row.names = FALSE
)

## 5. Export results as CSV
write.csv(
  clusters_final,
  file = "Genomic_clusters_HESN_vs_HIV_min3_gap1Mb.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)

## 6. Summarize genomic cluster characteristics by group
cluster_counts <- clusters_final %>%
  dplyr::group_by(Group) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    Number_of_clusters = dplyr::n(),
    Genes_in_clusters = sum(n_genes),
    Largest_cluster = max(n_genes),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(cluster_counts)
```

```{r}
################################################################################

## 3. Generate the sensitivity gene set

stopifnot(!any(genes_largest_cluster %in% genes_HESN_up_sensitivity))
stopifnot(all(genes_largest_cluster %in% genes_HESN_up))

## 4. Repeat the genomic clustering permutation test

  res_HESN_cluster$summary %>% dplyr::mutate(Analysis = "Original HESN-UP"),
  res_HESN_without_largest$summary %>% dplyr::mutate(Analysis = "HESN-UP without largest cluster")
) %>%
  dplyr::select(Analysis, dplyr::everything())

print(permutation_comparison, n = Inf, width = Inf)

## 7. Export sensitivity comparisons

write.table(permutation_comparison, "HESN_sensitivity_without_largest_cluster_permutation.tsv", sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r}
library(pROC)

## Use the same outcome for both models
## Ensure that the 56 external samples are in exactly the same order

y_ext <- y_external

roc_orig <- roc(
  response  = y_ext,
  predictor = as.numeric(prob_nuevas),
  levels = c(0, 1),
  direction = "<",
  quiet = TRUE
)

roc_trans <- roc(
  response  = y_ext,
  predictor = as.numeric(prob_external),
  levels = c(0, 1),
  direction = "<",
  quiet = TRUE
)

cat("Original model AUC      :", as.numeric(auc(roc_orig)), "\n")
cat("Transportable model AUC :", as.numeric(auc(roc_trans)), "\n")
cat("AUC difference          :",
    as.numeric(auc(roc_trans) - auc(roc_orig)), "\n")

test_delong <- roc.test(
  roc_orig,
  roc_trans,
  paired = TRUE,
  method = "delong"
)

print(test_delong)


set.seed(2026)

B <- 10000

idx0 <- which(y_ext == 0)
idx1 <- which(y_ext == 1)

delta_auc_boot <- numeric(B)

for (b in seq_len(B)) {

  ## Stratified and PAIRED bootstrap:
  ## resample exactly the same individuals for both models

  ib0 <- sample(idx0, length(idx0), replace = TRUE)
  ib1 <- sample(idx1, length(idx1), replace = TRUE)

  ib <- c(ib0, ib1)

  y_b <- y_ext[ib]

  roc_o_b <- roc(
    y_b,
    as.numeric(prob_nuevas)[ib],
    levels = c(0, 1),
    direction = "<",
    quiet = TRUE
  )

  roc_t_b <- roc(
    y_b,
    as.numeric(prob_external)[ib],
    levels = c(0, 1),
    direction = "<",
    quiet = TRUE
  )

  delta_auc_boot[b] <-
    as.numeric(auc(roc_t_b)) -
    as.numeric(auc(roc_o_b))
}

delta_auc_obs <-
  as.numeric(auc(roc_trans)) -
  as.numeric(auc(roc_orig))

ci_delta <- quantile(
  delta_auc_boot,
  probs = c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975),
  na.rm = TRUE
)

cat("\nObserved AUC difference =", round(delta_auc_obs, 4), "\n")
cat(
  "Bootstrap 95% CI =",
  round(ci_delta[1], 4), "to",
  round(ci_delta[3], 4), "\n"
)

## Proportion of bootstrap replicates in which TRANSPORTABLE > ORIGINAL
p_superior <- mean(delta_auc_boot > 0, na.rm = TRUE)

cat(
  "Bootstrap P(Delta AUC > 0) =",
  round(p_superior, 4),
  "\n"
)
```

```{r}
############################################################
## DE NOVO PREDICTIVE MODEL – GSE165132 ECTOCERVIX
## Raw RNA-seq counts
##
## Outcome:
##   HIV  = 0
##   HESN = 1
##
## Architecture mirroring the PBMC model:
## DESeq2 in-fold -> TMM/logCPM -> Elastic Net
## -> out-of-fold predictions
############################################################

library(glmnet)
library(pROC)
library(dplyr)
library(tibble)
library(DESeq2)
library(edgeR)
library(caret)


# ============================================================
# 1. LOAD DATA
# ============================================================

raw_cervix <- read.csv(
  "GSE165132_Raw_gene_counts_matrix.csv",
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
  check.names = FALSE
)

meta_cervix <- read.csv(
  "GSE165132_metadata.csv",
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
  check.names = FALSE
)

raw_cervix$symbol <- trimws(
  as.character(raw_cervix$symbol)
)

meta_cervix$subjectID <- trimws(
  as.character(meta_cervix$subjectID)
)

meta_cervix$group <- trimws(
  as.character(meta_cervix$group)
)


# ============================================================
# 2. REMOVE GENES WITH MISSING SYMBOLS
# ============================================================

bad_symbol <- is.na(raw_cervix$symbol) |
              raw_cervix$symbol == ""

cat(
  "Genes removed due to missing symbols:",
  sum(bad_symbol),
  "\n"
)

raw_cervix <- raw_cervix[
  !bad_symbol,
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]


# ============================================================
# 3. CHECK FOR GENUINE DUPLICATES
# ============================================================

dup_symbols <- unique(
  raw_cervix$symbol[
    duplicated(raw_cervix$symbol)
  ]
)

cat(
  "Genuinely duplicated gene symbols after removing missing/empty entries:",
  length(dup_symbols),
  "\n"
)

if (length(dup_symbols) > 0) {

  print(dup_symbols)

  stop(
    paste0(
      "Genuinely duplicated gene symbols were detected. ",
      "Do not proceed until they are resolved."
    )
  )
}


# ============================================================
# 4. BUILD RAW COUNT MATRIX
# ============================================================

annotation_cols <- c(
  "entrez",
  "symbol",
  "length"
)

sample_cols <- setdiff(
  colnames(raw_cervix),
  annotation_cols
)

mat_raw_cervix <- as.matrix(
  raw_cervix[
    ,
    sample_cols,
    drop = FALSE
  ]
)

storage.mode(mat_raw_cervix) <- "numeric"

rownames(mat_raw_cervix) <- raw_cervix$symbol


# Strict integrity checks

stopifnot(
  !anyNA(mat_raw_cervix),
  all(is.finite(mat_raw_cervix)),
  all(mat_raw_cervix >= 0),
  all(mat_raw_cervix == round(mat_raw_cervix))
)


# ============================================================
# 5. ALIGN METADATA EXACTLY WITH COUNT MATRIX
# ============================================================

stopifnot(
  setequal(
    colnames(mat_raw_cervix),
    meta_cervix$subjectID
  )
)

meta_cervix <- meta_cervix[
  match(
    colnames(mat_raw_cervix),
    meta_cervix$subjectID
  ),
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]

rownames(meta_cervix) <- meta_cervix$subjectID

stopifnot(
  identical(
    colnames(mat_raw_cervix),
    rownames(meta_cervix)
  )
)


# ============================================================
# 6. OUTCOME
# ============================================================

y_cervix <- factor(
  meta_cervix$group,
  levels = c("HIV", "HESN")
)

y_bin_cervix <- unname(
  ifelse(
    y_cervix == "HESN",
    1L,
    0L
  )
)

cat("\nOutcome distribution:\n")
print(table(y_cervix))

stopifnot(
  length(y_bin_cervix) ==
    ncol(mat_raw_cervix),

  length(unique(y_bin_cervix)) == 2
)


# ============================================================
# 7. OUTER CV — SAME DESIGN AS PBMC MODEL
# ============================================================

set.seed(123)

folds_cervix <- caret::createFolds(
  y_cervix,
  k = 5,
  list = TRUE, 
  returnTrain = FALSE
)

cervix_preds_min <- rep(
  NA_real_,
  length(y_bin_cervix)
)

cervix_preds_1se <- rep(
  NA_real_,
  length(y_bin_cervix)
)

cervix_used_planB <- rep(
  FALSE,
  length(folds_cervix)
)


# ============================================================
# 8. COEFFICIENT HISTORY
# ============================================================

cervix_coefficients_history <- data.frame(
  Fold = character(),
  Gene = character(),
  Beta = numeric(),
  Lambda = character(),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

cervix_deseq_history <- data.frame(
  Fold = character(),
  Gene = character(),
  Passed_DESeq = logical(),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)


# ============================================================
# 9. OUTER CV LOOP
# ============================================================

for (i in seq_along(folds_cervix)) {

  message(
    "\n=============================="
  )

  message(
    "CERVIX — Fold ",
    i,
    " of ",
    length(folds_cervix)
  )

  message(
    "=============================="
  )


  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # TRAIN / TEST
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  test_idx <- folds_cervix[[i]]

  train_idx <- setdiff(
    seq_along(y_bin_cervix),
    test_idx
  )

  X_raw_tr <- mat_raw_cervix[
    ,
    train_idx,
    drop = FALSE
  ]

  X_raw_te <- mat_raw_cervix[
    ,
    test_idx,
    drop = FALSE
  ]

  meta_tr <- meta_cervix[
    train_idx,
    ,
    drop = FALSE
  ]

  Y_tr_ml <- y_bin_cervix[
    train_idx
  ]


  cat(
    "Train:",
    length(train_idx),
    " Test:",
    length(test_idx),
    "\n"
  )

  print(
    table(
      meta_tr$group
    )
  )


  # ==========================================================
  # A. DESeq2 ON TRAINING DATA ONLY
  # ==========================================================

  meta_tr$group <- factor(
    meta_tr$group,
    levels = c("HIV", "HESN")
  )

  dds_tr <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(
    countData = round(X_raw_tr),
    colData = meta_tr,
    design = ~ group
  )


  # Same PBMC filter:
  # counts >= 10 in >= 5 training samples

  keep <- rowSums(
    counts(dds_tr) >= 10
  ) >= 5

  dds_tr <- dds_tr[
    keep,
  ]

  cat(
    "Genes retained after technical filtering:",
    nrow(dds_tr),
    "\n"
  )


  dds_tr <- DESeq(
    dds_tr,
    quiet = TRUE
  )


  # HESN vs HIV
  res_tr <- results(
    dds_tr,
    contrast = c(
      "group",
      "HESN",
      "HIV"
    )
  )


  res_tr_df <- as.data.frame(res_tr) %>%
  tibble::rownames_to_column("gene") %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(padj))


  # ==========================================================
  # B. SAME BIOLOGICAL FILTER AS PBMC MODEL
  # ==========================================================

  #sig_bio_fold <- res_tr_df %>%
   # filter(
    #  pvalue < 0.05,
     # abs(log2FoldChange) > 0    )

  #genes_ml_fold <- sig_bio_fold$gene


 # cat(    "Significant DE genes:",    length(genes_ml_fold),    "\n"  )

# No biological/supervised filtering:
# all genes passing the fold-specific technical filter
genes_ml_fold <- res_tr_df$gene

genes_ml_fold <- genes_ml_fold[
  !is.na(genes_ml_fold)
]

cat(
  "Candidate genes (without p-value filtering):",
  length(genes_ml_fold),
  "\n"
)
  # ==========================================================
  # C. SAME FALLBACK STRATEGY AS PBMC MODEL
  # ==========================================================

  if (length(genes_ml_fold) < 5) {

    cervix_used_planB[i] <- TRUE

    genes_ml_fold <- res_tr_df %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(pvalue)) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(pvalue) %>%
  dplyr::slice_head(n = 100) %>%
  dplyr::pull(gene)

    message(
      "Fallback activated: top 100 genes ranked by p-value."
    )
  }


  genes_ml_fold <- genes_ml_fold[
    genes_ml_fold %in%
      rownames(X_raw_te)
  ]


  if (length(genes_ml_fold) < 2) {

    stop(
      paste(
        "Fold",
        i,
        "has fewer than 2 genes."
      )
    )
  }


  # Record DESeq2 filtering results

  df_deseq_fold <- data.frame(
    Fold = paste0(
      "Fold_",
      i
    ),
    Gene = genes_ml_fold,
    Passed_DESeq = TRUE,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )

  cervix_deseq_history <- rbind(
    cervix_deseq_history,
    df_deseq_fold
  )


  # ==========================================================
  # D. TMM/logCPM — SAME PROTOCOL AS PBMC MODEL
  # ==========================================================

  base_genes <- rownames(
    dds_tr
  )


  # TRAIN

  dge_tr <- DGEList(
    counts =
      X_raw_tr[
        base_genes,
        ,
        drop = FALSE
      ]
  )

  dge_tr <- calcNormFactors(
    dge_tr,
    method = "TMM"
  )

  logCPM_tr <- cpm(
    dge_tr,
    log = TRUE,
    prior.count = 1
  )


  # TEST

  dge_te <- DGEList(
    counts =
      X_raw_te[
        base_genes,
        ,
        drop = FALSE
      ]
  )

  dge_te <- calcNormFactors(
    dge_te,
    method = "TMM"
  )

  logCPM_te <- cpm(
    dge_te,
    log = TRUE,
    prior.count = 1
  )


  # ==========================================================
  # E. ELASTIC NET MATRICES
  # ==========================================================

  X_tr_ml <- t(
    logCPM_tr[
      genes_ml_fold,
      ,
      drop = FALSE
    ]
  )

  X_te_ml <- t(
    logCPM_te[
      genes_ml_fold,
      ,
      drop = FALSE
    ]
  )

  gene_names_fold <- colnames(
    X_tr_ml
  )

  rownames(X_tr_ml) <- NULL
  rownames(X_te_ml) <- NULL


  stopifnot(
    nrow(X_tr_ml) ==
      length(Y_tr_ml),

    ncol(X_tr_ml) ==
      ncol(X_te_ml),

    identical(
      colnames(X_tr_ml),
      colnames(X_te_ml)
    )
  )


  # ==========================================================
  # F. INNER CV — ELASTIC NET
  # ==========================================================

  set.seed(
    1000 + i
  )

  cvfit_inner <- cv.glmnet(
    x = as.matrix(X_tr_ml),
    y = Y_tr_ml,
    family = "binomial",
    alpha = 0.5,
    nfolds = 3,
    type.measure = "deviance",
    standardize = TRUE
  )


  # ==========================================================
  # G. OOF PREDICTIONS
  # ==========================================================

  cervix_preds_min[
    test_idx
  ] <- as.numeric(
    predict(
      cvfit_inner,
      newx = as.matrix(X_te_ml),
      s = "lambda.min",
      type = "response"
    )
  )

  cervix_preds_1se[
    test_idx
  ] <- as.numeric(
    predict(
      cvfit_inner,
      newx = as.matrix(X_te_ml),
      s = "lambda.1se",
      type = "response"
    )
  )


  # ==========================================================
  # H. COEFFICIENT TRACKING
  # ==========================================================

  for (
    lambda_str in
    c(
      "lambda.min",
      "lambda.1se"
    )
  ) {

    coef_matrix <- as.matrix(
      coef(
        cvfit_inner,
        s = lambda_str
      )
    )

    df_fold_coefs <- data.frame(
      Fold = paste0(
        "Fold_",
        i
      ),

      Gene = rownames(
        coef_matrix
      ),

      Beta = as.numeric(
        coef_matrix[, 1]
      ),

      Lambda = lambda_str,

      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )

    cervix_coefficients_history <-
      rbind(
        cervix_coefficients_history,
        df_fold_coefs
      )
  }
}


# ============================================================
# 10. OOF INTEGRITY CHECK
# ============================================================

stopifnot(
  !anyNA(cervix_preds_min),
  !anyNA(cervix_preds_1se),

  length(cervix_preds_1se) ==
    length(y_bin_cervix)
)


# ============================================================
# 11. ROC OOF
# ============================================================

roc_cervix_min <- pROC::roc(
  response = y_bin_cervix,
  predictor = cervix_preds_min,
  levels = c(0, 1),
  direction = "<",
  quiet = TRUE
)

roc_cervix_1se <- pROC::roc(
  response = y_bin_cervix,
  predictor = cervix_preds_1se,
  levels = c(0, 1),
  direction = "<",
  quiet = TRUE
)


auc_cervix_min <- as.numeric(
  pROC::auc(
    roc_cervix_min
  )
)

auc_cervix_1se <- as.numeric(
  pROC::auc(
    roc_cervix_1se
  )
)


ci_cervix_min <- pROC::ci.auc(
  roc_cervix_min
)

ci_cervix_1se <- pROC::ci.auc(
  roc_cervix_1se
)


# ============================================================
# 12. RESULTS
# ============================================================

cat(
  "\n============================================\n"
)

cat(
  "DE NOVO ECTOCERVICAL MODEL — OOF\n"
)

cat(
  "============================================\n"
)

cat(
  "N =",
  length(y_bin_cervix),
  "\n"
)

cat(
  "HIV =",
  sum(y_bin_cervix == 0),
  "\n"
)

cat(
  "HESN =",
  sum(y_bin_cervix == 1),
  "\n\n"
)


cat(
  "lambda.min AUC:",
  round(auc_cervix_min, 3),
  "\n"
)

cat(
  "95% CI:",
  round(ci_cervix_min[1], 3),
  "-",
  round(ci_cervix_min[3], 3),
  "\n\n"
)


cat(
  "lambda.1se AUC:",
  round(auc_cervix_1se, 3),
  "\n"
)

cat(
  "95% CI:",
  round(ci_cervix_1se[1], 3),
  "-",
  round(ci_cervix_1se[3], 3),
  "\n\n"
)


cat(
  "Fallback used in",
  sum(cervix_used_planB),
  "of",
  length(folds_cervix),
  "folds\n"
)

cat(
  "============================================\n"
)


# ============================================================
# 13. OOF PREDICTION TABLE
# ============================================================

cervix_oof_predictions <- data.frame(
  subjectID =
    meta_cervix$subjectID,

  group =
    meta_cervix$group,

  y =
    y_bin_cervix,

  prob_lambda_min =
    cervix_preds_min,

  prob_lambda_1se =
    cervix_preds_1se,

  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)


# ============================================================
# 14. ATTRITION SUMMARY
# ============================================================

cervix_deseq_counts <-
  cervix_deseq_history %>%
  group_by(Gene) %>%
  summarise(
    Folds_Passed_DESeq =
      sum(Passed_DESeq),
    .groups = "drop"
  )


cervix_en_counts <- cervix_coefficients_history %>%
  dplyr::filter(Lambda == "lambda.1se", Gene != "(Intercept)") %>%
  dplyr::group_by(Gene) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    Folds_Selected_EN = sum(Beta != 0),
    Mean_Beta_Conditional = ifelse(any(Beta != 0), mean(Beta[Beta != 0]), NA_real_),
    Median_Beta_Conditional = ifelse(any(Beta != 0), median(Beta[Beta != 0]), NA_real_),
    .groups = "drop"
  )


cervix_pipeline_attrition <-
  full_join(
    cervix_deseq_counts,
    cervix_en_counts,
    by = "Gene"
  ) %>%
  mutate(

    Folds_Passed_DESeq =
      coalesce(
        Folds_Passed_DESeq,
        0L
      ),

    Folds_Selected_EN =
      coalesce(
        Folds_Selected_EN,
        0L
      ),

    Sign =
      case_when(

        Mean_Beta_Conditional > 0 ~
          "Up in HESN",

        Mean_Beta_Conditional < 0 ~
          "Up in HIV",

        TRUE ~
          NA_character_
      )
  ) %>%
  arrange(
    desc(Folds_Selected_EN),
    desc(Folds_Passed_DESeq),
    desc(
      abs(
        Median_Beta_Conditional
      )
    )
  )


cat(
  "\nTop 20 genes by OOF selection stability:\n"
)

print(
  as.data.frame(
    head(
      cervix_pipeline_attrition,
      100
    )
  )
)
```

```{r}

library(DESeq2)
library(edgeR)
library(glmnet)
library(caret)
library(pROC)
library(dplyr)

## Use the raw count matrix from the previous ectocervical analysis
counts_cervix <- mat_raw_cervix

stopifnot(
  identical(colnames(counts_cervix), rownames(meta_cervix)),
  identical(length(y_bin_cervix), ncol(counts_cervix))
)
# ==========================================================
# 1. GLOBAL DESeq2 — DELIBERATE DATA LEAKAGE
# ==========================================================

# Ensure identical sample ordering
stopifnot(
  identical(
    colnames(counts_cervix),
    rownames(meta_cervix)
  )
)

dds_leaky <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(
  countData = round(counts_cervix),
  colData   = meta_cervix,
  design    = ~ group
)

# Apply the same technical filtering criteria
keep_leaky <- rowSums(counts(dds_leaky) >= 10) >= 5
dds_leaky <- dds_leaky[keep_leaky, ]

dds_leaky <- DESeq(dds_leaky, quiet = TRUE)

res_leaky <- results(
  dds_leaky,
  contrast = c("group", "HESN", "HIV")
)

res_leaky_df <- as.data.frame(res_leaky)
res_leaky_df$gene <- rownames(res_leaky_df)

## Global supervised feature selection — deliberately leaky
genes_leaky <- res_leaky_df %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(pvalue), pvalue < 0.05) %>%
  dplyr::pull(gene)

cat("Genes selected GLOBALLY at p < 0.05:", length(genes_leaky), "\n")

head(
  res_leaky_df %>%
    dplyr::filter(gene %in% genes_leaky) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(pvalue),
  20
)
# ==========================================================
# 2. 10-FOLD CV USING GLOBALLY SELECTED FEATURES
#    !!! DELIBERATE FEATURE-SELECTION LEAKAGE !!!
# ==========================================================

set.seed(123)

folds_leaky <- caret::createFolds(
  y_cervix,
  k = 10,
  list = TRUE,
  returnTrain = FALSE
)

preds_leaky_min <- rep(NA_real_, length(y_cervix))
preds_leaky_1se <- rep(NA_real_, length(y_cervix))

selected_leaky <- vector("list", length(folds_leaky))

for (i in seq_along(folds_leaky)) {

  cat(
    "\n==============================\n",
    "LEAKY CERVIX — Fold", i, "of 10\n",
    "==============================\n"
  )

  idx_te <- folds_leaky[[i]]
  idx_tr <- setdiff(seq_along(y_cervix), idx_te)

  X_raw_tr <- counts_cervix[, idx_tr, drop = FALSE]
  X_raw_te <- counts_cervix[, idx_te, drop = FALSE]

  y_tr <- y_bin_cervix[idx_tr]

  cat(
    "Training:", length(idx_tr),
    " Test:", length(idx_te), "\n"
  )

  # ------------------------------------------
  # Use only genes previously selected
  # GLOBALLY across the entire dataset
  # ------------------------------------------

  genes_fold <- intersect(
    genes_leaky,
    rownames(X_raw_tr)
  )

  cat(
    "Globally selected candidate genes:",
    length(genes_fold),
    "\n"
  )

  # ------------------------------------------
  # TMM normalization / logCPM transformation
  # ------------------------------------------

  dge_tr <- DGEList(
    counts = X_raw_tr[
      genes_fold,
      ,
      drop = FALSE
    ]
  )

  dge_tr <- calcNormFactors(
    dge_tr,
    method = "TMM"
  )

  logCPM_tr <- cpm(
    dge_tr,
    log = TRUE,
    prior.count = 1
  )

  dge_te <- DGEList(
    counts = X_raw_te[
      genes_fold,
      ,
      drop = FALSE
    ]
  )

  dge_te <- calcNormFactors(
    dge_te,
    method = "TMM"
  )

  logCPM_te <- cpm(
    dge_te,
    log = TRUE,
    prior.count = 1
  )

  X_tr_ml <- t(logCPM_tr)
  X_te_ml <- t(logCPM_te)

  stopifnot(
    identical(
      colnames(X_tr_ml),
      colnames(X_te_ml)
    )
  )

  # ------------------------------------------
  # Elastic Net model fitting
  # ------------------------------------------

  set.seed(1000 + i)

  cvfit_leaky <- cv.glmnet(
    x = as.matrix(X_tr_ml),
    y = y_tr,
    family = "binomial",
    alpha = 0.5,
    nfolds = 3,
    type.measure = "deviance",
    standardize = TRUE
  )

  preds_leaky_min[idx_te] <- as.numeric(
    predict(
      cvfit_leaky,
      newx = as.matrix(X_te_ml),
      s = "lambda.min",
      type = "response"
    )
  )

  preds_leaky_1se[idx_te] <- as.numeric(
    predict(
      cvfit_leaky,
      newx = as.matrix(X_te_ml),
      s = "lambda.1se",
      type = "response"
    )
  )

  # Extract active genes at lambda.1se
  cf <- coef(
    cvfit_leaky,
    s = "lambda.1se"
  )

  active <- rownames(cf)[
    as.vector(cf != 0)
  ]

  active <- setdiff(
    active,
    "(Intercept)"
  )

  selected_leaky[[i]] <- active

  cat(
    "Active Elastic Net genes:",
    length(active),
    "\n"
  )
}

# ==========================================================
# 3. "OOF" AUC CONTAMINATED BY FEATURE-SELECTION LEAKAGE
# ==========================================================

stopifnot(
  !anyNA(preds_leaky_min),
  !anyNA(preds_leaky_1se)
)

roc_leaky_min <- pROC::roc(
  response = y_bin_cervix,
  predictor = preds_leaky_min,
  levels = c(0, 1),
  direction = "<",
  quiet = TRUE
)

roc_leaky_1se <- pROC::roc(
  response = y_bin_cervix,
  predictor = preds_leaky_1se,
  levels = c(0, 1),
  direction = "<",
  quiet = TRUE
)

cat(
  "\n============================================\n",
  "CERVIX — DELIBERATE LEAKAGE CONTROL\n",
  "============================================\n",
  "Globally selected genes:",
  length(genes_leaky), "\n\n",

  "lambda.min AUC:",
  round(as.numeric(auc(roc_leaky_min)), 3), "\n",
  "95% CI:",
  paste(
    round(as.numeric(ci.auc(roc_leaky_min)), 3),
    collapse = " - "
  ), "\n\n",

  "lambda.1se AUC:",
  round(as.numeric(auc(roc_leaky_1se)), 3), "\n",
  "95% CI:",
  paste(
    round(as.numeric(ci.auc(roc_leaky_1se)), 3),
    collapse = " - "
  ), "\n",
  "============================================\n"
)
```

```{r}

roc_ORIG17_PBMC <- roc_1se
roc_ORIG17_CERV <- roc_externo
roc_CC14_PBMC   <- roc_transport_oof
roc_CC14_CERV   <- roc_external_transport


draw_roc_panel <- function(roc_obj, panel, title) {

  auc_val <- as.numeric(pROC::auc(roc_obj))

  plot(
    roc_obj,
    legacy.axes = TRUE,
    col = "darkblue",
    lwd = 3,
    xlim = c(0, 1),
    ylim = c(0, 1),
    xaxs = "i",
    yaxs = "i",
    xlab = "1 - Specificity",
    ylab = "Sensitivity",
    main = "",
    asp = 1,
    axes = FALSE
  )

  axis(
    1,
    at = seq(0, 1, 0.2),
    labels = sprintf("%.1f", seq(0, 1, 0.2))
  )

  axis(
    2,
    at = seq(0, 1, 0.2),
    labels = sprintf("%.1f", seq(0, 1, 0.2)),
    las = 1
  )

  box()

  abline(
    a = 0,
    b = 1,
    col = "grey70",
    lwd = 1.3
  )

  mtext(
    panel,
    side = 3,
    adj = 0,
    line = 0.5,
    font = 2,
    cex = 1.2
  )

  mtext(
    title,
    side = 3,
    line = 0.5,
    cex = 1.05
  )

  legend(
    "bottomright",
    legend = sprintf("AUC = %.3f", auc_val),
    col = "darkblue",
    lwd = 3,
    bty = "n",
    cex = 1,
    inset = 0.02
  )
}


draw_roc_2x2 <- function() {

  par(
    mfrow = c(2, 2),
    mar = c(4.5, 4.5, 3.0, 1.2),
    oma = c(0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5)
  )

  draw_roc_panel(
    roc_ORIG17_PBMC,
    panel = "A",
    title = "ORIG17 — PBMC"
  )

  draw_roc_panel(
    roc_ORIG17_CERV,
    panel = "B",
    title = "ORIG17 — Ectocervix"
  )

  draw_roc_panel(
    roc_CC14_PBMC,
    panel = "C",
    title = "CC14 — PBMC"
  )

  draw_roc_panel(
    roc_CC14_CERV,
    panel = "D",
    title = "CC14 — Ectocervix"
  )
}


# Display the 2 × 2 ROC panel
draw_roc_2x2()


# Save the figure as a publication-quality TIFF
tiff("ROC_ORIG17_CC14_Clean_BaseR.tiff", width = 8, height = 8, units = "in", res = 300, compression = "lzw")

# Configure the 2 × 2 layout and margins (bottom, left, top, right)
par(mfrow = c(2, 2), mar = c(4.5, 4.5, 3, 1.5), oma = c(0, 0, 0, 0))

# Helper function to plot each ROC curve without overlapping annotations
plot_roc_base_clean <- function(roc_obj, main_title, panel_tag) {

  # 1. Plot the ROC curve without additional diagonal lines or grid lines
  plot(
    roc_obj,
    legacy.axes = TRUE,
    print.auc = TRUE,
    auc.polygon = FALSE,
    grid = FALSE,
    max.auc.polygon = FALSE,
    col = "#002B7F",
    lwd = 3,
    main = "",          # Suppress the automatic title
    xlab = "1 - Specificity",
    ylab = "Sensitivity",
    cex.lab = 1.1,
    cex.axis = 1.0
  )

  # 2. Add a centered title above the plot
  title(main = main_title, line = 1.2, cex.main = 1.2, font.main = 2)

  # 3. Position the panel label (A, B, C, D) in the upper-left margin without overlapping the curve
  mtext(panel_tag, side = 3, line = 1.2, at = -0.12, cex = 1.3, font = 2, xpd = TRUE)
}

# Generate the four ROC panels
plot_roc_base_clean(roc_ORIG17_PBMC, "ORIG17 — PBMC", "A")
plot_roc_base_clean(roc_ORIG17_CERV, "ORIG17 — Ectocervix", "B")
plot_roc_base_clean(roc_CC14_PBMC, "CC14 — PBMC", "C")
plot_roc_base_clean(roc_CC14_CERV, "CC14 — Ectocervix", "D")

dev.off()
```

```{r}


################################################################################
## AUC 95% CONFIDENCE INTERVALS AND MANUSCRIPT FIGURE LEGEND
## ORIG17 vs. CC14 — PBMC and ectocervix
################################################################################

library(pROC)

## 1. Use the existing ROC objects
roc_ORIG17_PBMC <- roc_1se
roc_ORIG17_CERV <- roc_externo
roc_CC14_PBMC <- roc_transport_oof
roc_CC14_CERV <- roc_external_transport

## 2. Calculate AUC and 95% CI directly from each ROC object
calc_auc_ci <- function(roc_obj, label) {
  auc_val <- as.numeric(pROC::auc(roc_obj))
  ci_res <- pROC::ci.auc(roc_obj, method = "delong")
  formatted <- sprintf("%.3f (95%% CI, %.3f–%.3f)", auc_val, ci_res[1], ci_res[3])
  cat(label, ": ", formatted, "\n", sep = "")
  return(list(roc = roc_obj, auc = auc_val, ci_lower = as.numeric(ci_res[1]), ci_upper = as.numeric(ci_res[3]), text = formatted))
}

## 3. Calculate results for the four panels
res_panelA <- calc_auc_ci(roc_ORIG17_PBMC, "A — ORIG17 / PBMC")
res_panelB <- calc_auc_ci(roc_ORIG17_CERV, "B — ORIG17 / Ectocervix")
res_panelC <- calc_auc_ci(roc_CC14_PBMC, "C — CC14 / PBMC")
res_panelD <- calc_auc_ci(roc_CC14_CERV, "D — CC14 / Ectocervix")

## 4. Export summary table
auc_summary <- data.frame(
  Panel = c("A", "B", "C", "D"),
  Classifier = c("ORIG17", "ORIG17", "CC14", "CC14"),
  Cohort = c("PBMC", "Ectocervix", "PBMC", "Ectocervix"),
  AUC = c(res_panelA$auc, res_panelB$auc, res_panelC$auc, res_panelD$auc),
  CI_lower = c(res_panelA$ci_lower, res_panelB$ci_lower, res_panelC$ci_lower, res_panelD$ci_lower),
  CI_upper = c(res_panelA$ci_upper, res_panelB$ci_upper, res_panelC$ci_upper, res_panelD$ci_upper)
)

print(auc_summary, row.names = FALSE)
write.table(auc_summary, "ROC_ORIG17_CC14_AUC_95CI.tsv", sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)

## 5. Generate manuscript figure legend
figure_legend <- paste0(
  "Figure X. Predictive performance and cross-cohort transportability of the gene classifiers. ",
  "Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves comparing the original 17-gene classifier (ORIG17) ",
  "and the transportability-constrained 14-gene classifier (CC14) across PBMC and ectocervical datasets. ",
  "(A) ORIG17 in PBMC: AUC = ", res_panelA$text, ". ",
  "(B) ORIG17 in ectocervix (GSE165132): AUC = ", res_panelB$text, ". ",
  "(C) CC14 in PBMC: AUC = ", res_panelC$text, ". ",
  "(D) CC14 in ectocervix (GSE165132): AUC = ", res_panelD$text, ". ",
  "AUC 95% confidence intervals were calculated using DeLong's method."
)

cat("\n============================================================\n")
cat("MANUSCRIPT FIGURE LEGEND\n")
cat("============================================================\n\n")
cat(figure_legend, "\n")

writeLines(figure_legend, "ROC_ORIG17_CC14_figure_legend.txt")

```

```{r}
# ============================================================
# FIGURE 6 — CC14
# OOF RISK SCORE AND TIME TO HIV-1 SEROCONVERSION
#
# A. Kaplan-Meier by OOF risk-score tertiles
# B. Time-varying HR per +1 SD in OOF risk score
# ============================================================

library(survival)
library(survminer)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(patchwork)


# ============================================================
# 1. CHECK CC14 OOF DATA
# ============================================================

# Expected object:
# df_surv_transport_oof
#
# Expected variables:
# TTS
# event
# Grupo_KM_transport_OOF

risk_levels <- c(
  "T1_LowRisk",
  "T2_MedRisk",
  "T3_HighRisk"
)

risk_labels <- c(
  "Low risk",
  "Intermediate risk",
  "High risk"
)

df_surv_transport_oof$Grupo_KM_transport_OOF <- factor(
  df_surv_transport_oof$Grupo_KM_transport_OOF,
  levels = risk_levels
)


cat("\n============================================\n")
cat("CC14 OOF — EVENTS BY RISK TERTILE\n")
cat("============================================\n")

print(
  table(
    df_surv_transport_oof$Grupo_KM_transport_OOF,
    df_surv_transport_oof$event
  )
)

# MUST give approximately:
#
#                    0    1
# T1_LowRisk       33    2
# T2_MedRisk       24   10
# T3_HighRisk       8   27


# ============================================================
# 2. KAPLAN-MEIER + LOG-RANK
# ============================================================

fit_CC14 <- survfit(
  Surv(TTS, event) ~ Grupo_KM_transport_OOF,
  data = df_surv_transport_oof
)

lr_CC14 <- survdiff(
  Surv(TTS, event) ~ Grupo_KM_transport_OOF,
  data = df_surv_transport_oof
)

p_CC14 <- pchisq(
  lr_CC14$chisq,
  df = length(lr_CC14$n) - 1,
  lower.tail = FALSE
)

cat("\n============================================\n")
cat("CC14 OOF — LOG-RANK\n")
cat("============================================\n")

cat(
  "Chi-square =", round(lr_CC14$chisq, 3),
  "\np =", format(p_CC14, scientific = TRUE),
  "\n"
)

# Expected:
# Chi-square ~46.7
# p ~7.14e-11


# ============================================================
# 3. PANEL A — KAPLAN-MEIER
# ============================================================

km_CC14 <- ggsurvplot(
  fit_CC14,
  data = df_surv_transport_oof,

  # Risk table
  risk.table = TRUE,
  risk.table.height = 0.24,
  risk.table.col = "strata",

  # Curves
  conf.int = FALSE,
  censor = TRUE,
  censor.shape = 3,
  censor.size = 2.5,

  palette = c(
    "#2166AC",   # Low risk
    "#F4A261",   # Intermediate
    "#B2182B"    # High risk
  ),

  # Log-rank
  pval = paste0("Log-rank p = ", format(p_CC14, scientific = TRUE, digits = 3)),
  pval.coord = c(60, 0.18),

  # Axes
  xlim = c(0, 1200),
  break.time.by = 300,
  ylim = c(0, 1.02),

  xlab = "Follow-up time (days)",
  ylab = "Probability of remaining HIV-1 seronegative",

  # Legend
  legend.title = "Risk-score tertile",
  legend.labs = risk_labels,

  # Title
  title = "CC14 risk-score tertiles",

  # Theme
  ggtheme = theme_bw(base_size = 11),

  # Risk-table labels/colors
  risk.table.y.text = TRUE,
  risk.table.y.text.col = TRUE,

  tables.theme = theme_cleantable(base_size = 9)
)


# Add panel letter A ONLY to KM plot
km_CC14$plot <- km_CC14$plot +
  labs(tag = "A") +
  theme(
    plot.tag = element_text(
      face = "bold",
      size = 16
    ),
    plot.title = element_text(
      face = "bold",
      size = 13,
      hjust = 0.5
    ),
    legend.position = "right"
  )


# Don't modify axis.text.y here:
# survminer defines it internally and ggplot2 may throw
# the "Can't merge axis.text.y" error.

km_CC14$table <- km_CC14$table +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    axis.title.x = element_blank()
  )


# ============================================================
# 4. COX MODEL — CC14 OOF
# ============================================================

# This uses the SAME OOF score used in the definitive analysis.
#
# Expected object:
# df_transport_clean
#
# Expected variables:
# TTS
# event
# en_score_transport_z
# age
# risk

cox_CC14 <- coxph(
  Surv(TTS, event) ~
    en_score_transport_z +
    age +
    risk +
    tt(en_score_transport_z),

  data = df_transport_clean,

  tt = function(x, t, ...) {
    x * log(t + 1)
  },

  x = TRUE
)

cat("\n============================================\n")
cat("CC14 OOF — TIME-VARYING COX\n")
cat("============================================\n")

print(summary(cox_CC14))

# Expected approximately:
#
# en_score_transport_z       beta = -1.786253
# tt(en_score_transport_z)   beta =  0.491095
# interaction p = 0.00855
#
# Concordance = 0.800


# ============================================================
# 5. CALCULATE HR(t) AND 95% CI
# ============================================================

make_HRt <- function(
  model,
  score_name,
  tt_name,
  max_day = 1200
) {

  b <- coef(model)
  V <- vcov(model)

  times <- seq(1, max_day, by = 1)

  log_time <- log(times + 1)

  beta  <- b[score_name]
  gamma <- b[tt_name]

  # log HR(t)
  logHR <- beta + gamma * log_time

  # Variance including covariance between
  # beta and the time-interaction coefficient
  var_logHR <-
    V[score_name, score_name] +
    (log_time^2) * V[tt_name, tt_name] +
    2 * log_time * V[score_name, tt_name]

  se_logHR <- sqrt(var_logHR)

  tibble(
    Time = times,
    HR = exp(logHR),
    lower = exp(logHR - 1.96 * se_logHR),
    upper = exp(logHR + 1.96 * se_logHR)
  )
}


hr_CC14 <- make_HRt(
  model = cox_CC14,
  score_name = "en_score_transport_z",
  tt_name = "tt(en_score_transport_z)",
  max_day = 1200
)


# ============================================================
# 6. VALUES TO ANNOTATE
# ============================================================

# Four representative follow-up times.
# If the plot looks crowded, remove 730.

key_times <- c(
  180,
  365,
  730,
  1095
)

ann_CC14 <- hr_CC14 %>%
  dplyr::filter(Time %in% key_times) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    label = sprintf("HR %.2f\n(%.2f–%.2f)", HR, lower, upper)
  )


cat("\n============================================\n")
cat("CC14 OOF — SELECTED HR(t)\n")
cat("============================================\n")

print(ann_CC14)


# ============================================================
# 7. CALCULATE HR = 1 CROSSING
# ============================================================

beta_CC14 <- coef(cox_CC14)["en_score_transport_z"]

gamma_CC14 <- coef(cox_CC14)[
  "tt(en_score_transport_z)"
]

cross_day_CC14 <-
  exp(-beta_CC14 / gamma_CC14) - 1

cat(
  "\nHR(t) crosses HR = 1 at approximately day",
  round(cross_day_CC14, 1),
  "\n"
)

# Expected ~37 days


# ============================================================
# 8. PANEL B — TIME-VARYING HR(t)
# ============================================================

hrplot_CC14 <- ggplot(
  hr_CC14,
  aes(x = Time, y = HR)
) +

  # 95% CI
  geom_ribbon(
    aes(
      ymin = lower,
      ymax = upper
    ),
    fill = "#2166AC",
    alpha = 0.18
  ) +

  # HR(t)
  geom_line(
    color = "#2166AC",
    linewidth = 1.1
  ) +

  # Null effect
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 1,
    linetype = "dashed",
    color = "grey40",
    linewidth = 0.7
  ) +

  # Selected time points
  geom_point(
    data = ann_CC14,
    aes(
      x = Time,
      y = HR
    ),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    color = "#B2182B",
    size = 2.5
  ) +

  # Numerical HR + CI
  geom_text(
    data = ann_CC14,
    aes(
      x = Time,
      y = upper,
      label = label
    ),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    vjust = -0.35,
    size = 3.1,
    fontface = "bold"
  ) +

  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = c(
      0,
      300,
      600,
      900,
      1200
    ),
    limits = c(
      0,
      1200
    ),
    expand = expansion(
      mult = c(0, 0.03)
    )
  ) +

  scale_y_continuous(
    expand = expansion(
      mult = c(0.03, 0.20)
    )
  ) +

  labs(
    tag = "B",

    title =
      "Time-varying effect of the CC14 risk score",

    x =
      "Follow-up time (days)",

    y =
      "Hazard ratio per 1-SD increase\nin OOF risk score"
  ) +

  theme_bw(
    base_size = 11
  ) +

  theme(
    plot.tag = element_text(
      face = "bold",
      size = 16
    ),

    plot.title = element_text(
      face = "bold",
      size = 13,
      hjust = 0.5
    ),

    panel.grid.minor =
      element_blank()
  )


# ============================================================
# 9. CREATE PANEL A AS A SINGLE BLOCK
# ============================================================

# IMPORTANT:
# wrap_plots() encapsulates KM + risk table so patchwork
# treats them together when Figure 6 is assembled.

panel_A <- wrap_plots(
  km_CC14$plot,
  km_CC14$table,

  ncol = 1,

  heights = c(
    3.5,
    1
  )
)


# ============================================================
# 10. PANEL B
# ============================================================

panel_B <- hrplot_CC14


# ============================================================
# 11. FINAL FIGURE — VERTICAL
# ============================================================

Figure6_CC14 <- wrap_plots(
  panel_A,
  panel_B,

  ncol = 1,

  heights = c(
    1.20,
    1
  )
) +

  plot_annotation(
    title =
      "Association of the transcriptional risk score with time to HIV-1 seroconversion",

    theme = theme(
      plot.title = element_text(
        face = "bold",
        size = 15,
        hjust = 0.5
      )
    )
  )


# Show figure
Figure6_CC14


# ============================================================
# 12. EXPORT — PDF
# ============================================================

ggsave(
  filename =
    "Figure6_CC14_Time_to_Seroconversion.pdf",

  plot =
    Figure6_CC14,

  device =
    cairo_pdf,

  width =
    8,

  height =
    10.5,

  units =

)

ggsave(
```
